key_insight: Physical activity shares substantial genetic influences with schizophrenia and Parkinson’s disease despite negligible overall genetic correlations, reflecting mixed effect directions.
clinical_relevance: The findings offer biological context for studying physical activity as a candidate digital biomarker in neuropsychiatric disorders, not evidence for cancer drug discovery or clinical use.
method: Enhanced objectively measured activity GWAS with self-reported activity data.
Compared activity genetics with schizophrenia and Parkinson’s disease GWAS.
Combined causal mixture modelling, local genetic correlations and conjunctional false discovery rate analysis.
evidence_signal: Analyses included 89,683 participants with objectively measured activity and large disorder GWAS, finding substantial polygenic overlap despite genetic correlations of −0.02 to 0.02 (p > 0.05).
watch_item: Shared genetic architecture does not establish causality or validate physical activity for individual diagnosis or monitoring.
paper_title: Polygenic overlap of physical activity with schizophrenia and Parkinson's disease
